minutes.headline: Council on Aging hired a new full-time outreach worker and began setting rules for honorary board membership.
minutes.summary: The Lunenburg Council on Aging covered routine business: starting criteria for honorary membership (with a past chair nominated for the honor), a financial/personnel update including a new full-time outreach worker starting March 23, and a new senior-volunteer reading partnership with the elementary schools launching in the fall. The board also heard updates on a telehealth grant, a request to raise the center's programming budget to match the library's, a proposal to let seniors sponsor trip costs for others, and a fundraising report from the Eagle House Supporters.

what_happened.line: The Council on Aging reported hiring a new full-time outreach worker, starting March 23.
The board deferred finalizing honorary membership criteria to its next meeting, after nominating a past chair for the honor.
The director asked the town manager to raise the center's programming budget line to match increases given to the library.
The board agreed to let seniors sponsor another senior's cost on program and trip sign-up forms.
The caregiver resource connection program update was tabled pending the return of the staff member who oversees it.

why_it_matters: A new full-time outreach position affects the town's personnel budget and the level of direct service the senior center can offer residents.
A request to raise the center's programming line is a budget ask that would need town approval and affects funding parity across departments.
The sponsor-a-senior option and the tabled caregiver program both touch how accessible center services are to residents who need them most.
watch_next: Next Council on Aging meeting: finalized honorary membership criteria and a vote on the nominated honorary member
Status update on the caregiver resource connection program once the responsible staff member returns
